comparator.name: Earth Sciences (Aardwetenschappen)
comparator.sourceNotes: Dutch, full-time BSc Aardwetenschappen, VU Amsterdam, programme code 56986. The adopted 2026–27 OER governs this comparison. Aardoppervlak is the first-listed of two formal second-year routes, selected independently of UCR fit. Year 1: 60 compulsory EC. Year 2: 39 common plus 21 prescribed Aardoppervlak EC. Year 3: Hydrology 6, Philosophy/History of Science 6, thesis 18 and genuinely open academic profiling 30 EC. Zero-credit language and study/career requirements are additional obligations, not extra EC. The guide uses Aarde & Klimaat in prose, but the OER supplies the route name and units. Current marketing explicitly concerns the revised 2027–28 programme; its new course list is not imported. The 1 September 2026 announcement confirms continuation and phased renewal from September 2027. Visible OER headers/tables and PDF metadata identify the same 2026–27 edition.

trace: Introduces rocks/minerals, tectonics, seismology, stratigraphy and Earth systems, with actual Ardennes geological observation, mapping, cross-sections and stratigraphic reconstruction. This is substantial introductory geological practice, not the sustained specialist VU sequence.
introduces planetary boundaries and sustainability context; it is not a physical geology course
studies biodiversity, taxonomy and phylogeny; historical references to palaeontology do not supply a fossil or palaeontological sequence
applies geoscience principles to natural hazards, climate and resource risks; it is not a geomorphology sequence
models interactions among Earth spheres and studies climate proxies and isotope tracers
supplies general calculus, differential equations and complex-number tools; Earth-specific applications are not guaranteed
supplies general research design, statistics and group research practice; an Earth-science research subject is not guaranteed
studies physical climate drivers, greenhouse gases, ocean acidification and feedbacks alongside impacts and societal responses
introduces nature-based construction and Zeeland landscape, ecosystem and planning context; it is not specialist coastal geomorphology
supplies waves, chemistry and materials foundations for later environmental courses; its reflective and greenwashing work is not subsurface analysis
supplies general Python and discrete-mathematical programming tools; an Earth-model project is not guaranteed
Uses ArcGIS Pro spatial analysis, georeferencing, remote-sensing preprocessing and image processing in an environmental case study.

Uses soil coring, chemistry, microscopy, ICP interpretation and seismic, electrical-resistivity and electromagnetic field surveys to investigate soils and shallow aquifers. These are real field/laboratory and applied-geophysics methods, without the complete VU specialist sequence.
studies delta water management, salinisation, subsidence, freshwater scarcity and ecological/social choices; it is not a full physical-hydrology sequence
supplies general data cleaning, spatial/text analysis and visualisation; a particular Earth dataset is not guaranteed

Studies near-surface geochemical equilibrium, speciation, carbonate/redox chemistry, weathering and biomineralization using laboratory investigations and geochemical modelling. These substantively address environmental geochemistry rather than deep-rock petrology.
develops resource recovery/remediation and inorganic-chemistry laboratory skills; it is not specialist mineralogy or petrology

Applies spatial engineering, GIS and remote sensing to disaster response, agriculture, resources and environmental monitoring; projects give a specific complementary application of Earth-observation evidence.
develops general probability, sampling, estimation and simulation after calculus; Earth-specific data are not guaranteed
uses geoscience literature/research on geothermal energy, waste storage and carbon capture, with reports and conference-style presentation; hydrogen storage is not guaranteed
analyses renewable-energy technology, efficiency and technical-economic choices; it is context rather than geological site investigation

Evaluates solar, wind, hydro, geothermal and biomass resources, storage and grids through resource/yield calculations, Polysun modelling and practical mini-grid work; supports the evidenced geothermal/resource question, not subsurface geological-site training.
studies sustainability governance and policy tools through food, water, energy and climate problems; subsurface-specific governance is not guaranteed

alternatives.label: Earth systems, water and surface resources
alternatives.concept: Studies Earth spheres, past and future climate, geological and soil field evidence, aquifers, environmental geochemistry and satellite observation. Spatial planning applies this evidence to environmental problems; energy systems add a specific resource and geothermal application. Quantitative and computational tools support this Earth-science backbone. It does not reproduce VU’s sustained specialist geology and field sequence or its individual thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Seven ENVI courses (52.5 EC) provide direct Earth-science substance, complemented by climate science and water management. The label limits the comparison to this surface/system response and does not promise a specialist geology programme.
progression: Current formal offerings and earlier prerequisites pass. Sustainability Essentials I precedes Earth-system tools and chemistry/materials, which precede Spatial Planning, resource recovery and Earth resources. Dynamic Earth is available from semester 3; its geological foundations precede advanced geochemistry/resources, while prior Earth-system tools and hazards are permissible introductory study. Mathematics precedes probability. No additional prerequisites inferred from legacy outline codes. General research design and statistics now precede the advanced probability and applied project courses; later hazards applies preceding Earth-system and geospatial foundations.

routeSelection.basis: The 2026–27 OER confirms two formal tracks; neither is uniquely representative of the broad Earth Sciences target. The first-listed Aardoppervlak track is chosen under the neutral order tie-break and its complete 60-EC second-year path is used. The choice was made without considering UCR fit.

selection.assessment: One qualified Earth-system and surface-resource response is supported by seven direct Earth-science courses, real introductory geological field practice, soil/geophysical laboratory work, climate, geospatial and quantitative methods. Specialist geology/tectonics and sustained field-mapping candidates lack the advanced disciplinary sequence needed for another coherent 24-course response. A computational climate variant was reconsidered: this completed response already includes Python, R/data science, mathematics, probability, system tools and geospatial practice; arbitrary substitution of generic computing courses would not establish another distinct Earth-science priority. Geothermal/energy work is now implemented concretely, not used to manufacture an extra alternative. Historical hydrogen, Arctic and planetary examples remain search context and do not generate construction.

notes.text: VU requires a sustained specialist sequence in geology, geomorphology and geological fieldwork. UCR contributes real introductory geological mapping, rock and mineral identification, stratigraphy and field reporting, plus substantial soil, geochemical and applied-geophysical work. It offers less specialist depth and a shorter geological field sequence.

VU requires an 18 EC Earth-science thesis, including individual research, planning and scientific writing. This UCR schedule has no guaranteed independent Earth-science thesis. Optional independent research is shown separately, requires approval and is excluded from the scheduled 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Earth Sciences studies the Earth from its interior to its atmosphere through geology, climate, landscapes, chemistry, mathematics and field evidence. The selected Aardoppervlak route adds geomorphology and Dutch landscape development, an excursion and Jura fieldwork/reporting. The degree retains specialist geological training, open academic study space and an 18 EC Earth-science thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers one qualified direction in Earth systems, water and surface resources. Seven Earth-science courses provide a substantial backbone, including introductory geological mapping and field reporting, soil and aquifer analysis, geochemistry, climate and observation. Spatial planning, energy and quantitative methods support this response. The sustained specialist geology and field sequence and the 18 EC individual VU thesis remain substantial differences. Optional independent research is separate and requires approval.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 60 compulsory first-year EC, 39 common second-year EC plus 21 prescribed Aardoppervlak EC, and third-year Hydrology 6, Philosophy/History of Science 6, thesis 18 and open profiling 30 EC. Open individual choices require prior board approval, at least 12 EC at level 300 and at most 6 EC at level 100; listed or university minors can be exempt from prior approval if entry requirements are met. Foreign choices follow these levels and may include at most one 6 EC master course, not reusable in a later master. Jumilla fieldwork requires 15 programmed first-year EC passed before 1 March; its report follows the fieldwork. The second-year excursion and Jura fieldwork require 54 compulsory programmed EC and the Jumilla report passed before 1 February. The Jura report follows the fieldwork and must be passed before the thesis. The thesis page also requires February registration and approved agreement forms; the Jura report page states a 1 March passing deadline. These are distinct published administrative statements, not a relaxed prerequisite. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 42 EC, subject to exceptions. Dutch language testing and required remediation are integrated into Plate Tectonics without extra EC. The zero-credit year-two study/career course requires attendance, assignments, a LinkedIn profile and a networking report. Practical/workgroup attendance may apply as specified in course manuals. Optional honours and other routes are not stacked.

componentNotes.y3-03: Required 18 EC thesis: 1 EC planning, 2 EC scientific writing, 15 EC individual research/analysis/reporting/presentation. Practical research may be independent or in a small group; a short field, lab or modelling study may be included. Passed Jura report is the binding OER prerequisite. The thesis page requires field-report registration and approved agreement forms by 1 February and agreement submission before research. The report page separately mentions passing by 1 March. Both published conditions are retained; neither removes the passed-report prerequisite.
componentNotes.y3-04: Open academic profiling/minor space; at least 12 EC level 300 and at most 6 EC level 100 for individual choices. Prior approval applies except eligible university/listed minors. No particular optional minor is imposed.
componentNotes.y2-12: Prescribed Aardoppervlak route unit, not a free choice. Requires at least 54 compulsory programmed EC and a passed Jumilla report before 1 February.
componentNotes.y2-13: Prescribed Aardoppervlak fieldwork, with the same 54 EC and Jumilla-report conditions.
componentNotes.y2-14: Required report after Jura fieldwork; timely chapters and peer feedback compulsory. Draft and final each count 50%. Passed report required before thesis.
componentNotes.y1-12: Includes mandatory Dutch diagnostic language test and required remediation, without extra EC.
componentNotes.y1-14: At least 15 programmed first-year EC passed before 1 March; the separate report follows in year two.
